t.1.211.1: Vaiśaṃpāyana said: Then, after a few days, O king, there took place on that Mount Raivataka a very great festival of the Vṛṣṇis and Andhakas.
t.1.211.2: There, at that time, during the festival of that mountain, the heroes of the Bhojas, Vṛṣṇis and Andhakas gave gifts to the brāhmaṇas by the thousands.
t.1.211.3: All around that mountain, O king, the region was adorned with palaces variegated with jewels, and everywhere with lamp-trees.
t.1.211.4: And there the musicians played their instruments together; the dancers danced, and the singers sang songs.
t.1.211.5: And the adorned princes of the Vṛṣṇis, of very great vigor, roamed about everywhere in carriages whose bodies were brightly decorated with gold.
t.1.211.6: And the townspeople too came, on foot and in carriages of every kind, with their wives and with their retinues, by hundreds and then by thousands.
t.1.211.7: Then the lord Haladhara, intoxicated and accompanied by Revatī, roamed about there, O Bhārata, followed by Gandharvas.
t.1.211.8: Likewise came Ugrasena, the mighty king of the Vṛṣṇis, being sung of by Gandharvas and accompanied by a thousand women.
t.1.211.9: Raukmiṇeya and Sāmba, both intoxicated and fierce in battle, wearing celestial garlands and garments, sported about like two immortals.
t.1.211.10: Akrūra and Sāraṇa, Gada, Bhānu and Vidūratha, Niśaṭha and Cārudeṣṇa, Pṛthu and Vipṛthu as well.
t.1.211.12: These, each surrounded separately by women and Gandharvas, then adorned that festival on Raivataka.
t.1.211.11: Satyaka and Sātyaki too, Bhaṅgakāra and Sahācara, Hārdikya Kṛtavarman, and others who have not been named here.
t.1.211.13: Then, while that most auspicious tumult was going on, Vāsudeva and Pārtha wandered about together.
t.1.211.15: As soon as he saw her, love arose in Arjuna; Kṛṣṇa noticed Pārtha, his mind thus wholly fixed upon one object.
t.1.211.14: As the two of them were strolling about there, they then saw the lovely and auspicious daughter of Vasudeva, adorned with ornaments, in the midst of her friends.
t.1.211.18: Daughter of Vasudeva and sister of Vāsudeva, and endowed with beauty as well, whom indeed would she not bewitch?
t.1.211.19: Surely all my good fortune would be fully accomplished if this Vārṣṇeyī, your sister, were to become my queen.
t.1.211.20: But what means might there be for winning her? Tell me that, Janārdana. I shall undertake it all, if it can be done by a man.
t.1.211.22: And for heroic kṣatriyas, carrying off a bride by force for the sake of marriage is also praised; so those who know dharma understand.
t.1.211.24: Then Arjuna and Kṛṣṇa, having decided upon what was to be done, O king, at that time sent forth swift-moving men.
t.1.211.21: The svayaṃvara is the marriage of kṣatriyas, O bull among men; but it is uncertain, Pārtha, because a person's disposition cannot be predicted.
t.1.211.23: So you, Arjuna, carry off my lovely sister by force, for at a svayaṃvara who indeed knows what she intends to do?
t.1.211.17: This is my sister, Pārtha, the full sister of Sāraṇa. If your mind is set on her, I will speak to my father myself.
t.1.211.16: Then the lotus-eyed one, as if laughing, said, O Bhārata: "What is this, that the mind of a forest-dweller is stirred up by desire?"
t.1.211.25: All of that was made known to the Dharmarāja, who was in Indraprastha; and as soon as he heard it, that mighty-armed Pāṇḍava gave his consent.
